newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks plunge below 8,000 in China reaction.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks plunge below 8,000 in China reaction.

text.p: Taiwan share prices plunged to close below the 8,000 mark on Monday, shocked by a report that China would mount war games, possibly to protest a Taiwan visit by Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama.

At the close, the index had lost 3.49 percent or 287.19 points to 7,946.88 in the market's biggest single-session plunge since the last round of military tensions with arch rival China in early 1996, when it fell 346.74 points on January 5, 1996.
Turnover was an active T$124.8 billion.
The United Daily News reported that China planned to hold a joint-forces military exercise in April in coastal Fujian, Guangdong and Zhejiang provinces -- those nearest to Taiwan.
The report said the war games possibly were intended as a protest against the Dalai Lama's current visit in Taiwan.
"Rumours of an impending exercise have permeated the market," said Wang Jieh, analyst for Foremost Investment.

Brokers added that market sentiment was dampened further by a newspaper report that Morgan Stanley had lowered its suggested investment portfolio weighing for its investors in Taiwan stocks to four percent from an original six percent.
"There were many pieces of bearish news, and also, from a technical standpoint, the time was ripe for a fall," said Lin Long-hsien, analyst for United Securities.

Brokers said a recent outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease among the island's large hog population and a costly ban on pork exports would continue to deter buying interest in related food and livestock shares.
Food shares fell 3.82 percent, with Taiwan Tea plunging T$8 or the daily seven percent limit to T$109.
Plastics fell 4.26 percent, with Formosa Plastics losing T$3 to close at T$71.50.
